stemMd: Why does the author say that reuse involves more than “old walls”?

options.label: A
options.textMd: To include surrounding activities and timing within the design problem

options.label: B
options.textMd: To exclude access from architectural decisions

options.label: C
options.textMd: To argue that walls have no architectural significance

options.label: D
options.textMd: To demand demolition of every warehouse

options.label: E
options.textMd: To claim that schedules are permanent natural laws

explanationMd: The phrase broadens reuse beyond the retained physical shell. The example shows that spatial access and temporal coordination can determine whether a new use works within an existing urban setting.

distractorRationale.c: The identity and structure of the building still matter.
distractorRationale.d: The example develops a reuse solution.
distractorRationale.e: The planners deliberately revise the schedule.
distractorRationale.b: Access is explicitly treated as a design decision.
